record.original_question: If the geodesic flow of a Riemannian metric on the torus T^2 admits an integral that is polynomial of degree 3 in the velocities, then the metric admits a Killing vector field.

evidence.quote: If the geodesic flow of a Riemannian metric on the torus T^2 admits an integral that is polynomial of degree 3 in the velocities, then the metric admits a Killing vector field.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on the two-dimensional torus $T^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$, and let $\phi_t : TT^2 \to TT^2$ denote its geodesic flow. A function $F : TT^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is called an integral of the geodesic flow if $F$ is constant along every orbit of $\phi_t$. Such an integral is said to be polynomial of degree $n$ in the velocities if, in any local coordinate system $(x^1,x^2)$ on $T^2$ with corresponding fiber coordinates $(v^1,v^2)$ on $TT^2$, $F$ has the form $F(x,v) = \sum_{i_1+\cdots+i_n \le n} a_{i_1\cdots i_n}(x)\, v^{i_1}\cdots v^{i_n}$ with the top-degree homogeneous part not identically zero. A Killing vector field on $(T^2,g)$ is a vector field $X$ whose flow consists of isometries; equivalently, the symmetric part of $\nabla X$ vanishes. Equivalently, $X$ corresponds to an integral of the geodesic flow that is linear (polynomial of degree $1$) in the velocities.

Prove or disprove: if the geodesic flow of $(T^2,g)$ admits a non-trivial integral that is polynomial of degree $3$ in the velocities (functionally independent of the energy $|v|_g^2$), then $(T^2,g)$ admits a non-trivial Killing vector field.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that a Riemannian metric on $T^2$ whose geodesic flow admits a cubic polynomial integral must admit a Killing vector field is a long-standing open problem. Recent work (Bialy–Mironov; Sharafutdinov 2020; and others) makes partial progress: e.g., Bialy–Mironov reduce the question to a quasilinear system and show that any new integrable examples must lie in its region of hyperbolicity; Moroianu and others establish the result under additional symmetry/conformal assumptions. No general proof or counterexample is known as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Cubic and quartic integrals for geodesic flow on 2-torus via a system of the hydrodynamic type (Bialy–Mironov)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the classical question of polynomial-in-momenta integrals for geodesic flows on T^2; analyses the cubic case via a quasilinear system and shows new integrable examples can occur only in the hyperbolic region.
status_evidence.claim: The cubic-integral case on T^2 remains an open classical question with only partial reductions known.

status_evidence.title: Killing tensor fields of third rank on a two-dimensional Riemannian torus (Sharafutdinov, arXiv:2011.09603)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies rank-3 Killing tensors on the 2-torus and obtains partial results toward the conjecture that they reduce to symmetric products of Killing vector fields and the metric.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial results, but the cubic conjecture is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On first integrals of geodesic flows on a two-torus (Proc. Steklov Inst.)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style discussion confirming the cubic-integral question on T^2 remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Open problem status confirmed by recent surveys.
